description: The Yale New Haven Health study team released processed emergency-department visit data and R analysis scripts for a triage admission-prediction study. The repository README identifies a de-identified RData table with 560,486 visits and 972 variables. The paper says adult visits came from one academic, one community and one freestanding emergency department between March 2014 and July 2017. Variables include triage measures, prior use, demographics and processed clinical-history features; the outcome is admission or discharge. The raw electronic health records are withheld because of protected health information. The versioned Zenodo release provides a DOI and archived code and data, but this review read metadata only and did not download the 100 MB archive or the tracked RData file. Zenodo labels the release other-open without detailed licence text, and GitHub declares no separate licence; downstream redistribution terms need checking. Its regional, three-department coverage limits transfer to other hospitals. A modeller could use observed admission fractions and visit features to test ED-to-ward demand scenarios after checking de-identification, variable definitions and sampling. This resource complements data-cms-provider-data-hospitals, which describes public facility measures, not patient-level transitions.
licence: Zenodo registry classifies the release as other-open; no detailed redistribution licence is displayed. The GitHub repository has no declared licence; README asks users to cite the paper.
